core.title: Keep hand-authored plan unit specs schema-valid
core.given: A plan session where you hand-author unit specs of any authorable kind.
core.when: You add or re-state a unit while drafting, or ratify the session before the lock.
core.then: Keep every unit spec valid against its artifact schema: carried values well-formed (pattern, enum, type, additionalProperties) while drafting; kept units complete (required, minItems, minLength, minProperties) at ratification, before the lock.
prefer: Fix malformed values as soon as the drafting pass refuses them; re-state the unit (an upsert keyed by its reference) as it fills in.
Complete every kept unit before ratification. A kind blocks when its schema describes the artifacts the authoring tool actually authors.
For a kind with no schema, rely on its writer's validator; if nothing checks it, say so explicitly.
avoid: Treating an unfinished draft as a defect during drafting, or a malformed value as fine because it is a draft.
Ratifying with failing enforced or promoted-kind specs; a failure leaves the session unlocked.
Reading a clean result from an ungoverned kind as approval.
unless: Advisory kinds — whose schema has drifted from what the authoring tool authors — report and never block; findings ride on the unit, survive session-history compaction and resurface at ratification. A repository may promote a kind to enforced via its configuration.
core.why: The authoring tool emits artifacts that are schema-valid by construction; plan unit specs are hand-written, so this layer must keep that guarantee. Silence that reads as approval is the defect this rule prevents.
evidence: The drafting pass refuses malformed carried values of enforced kinds the moment they are written.
The ratification pass validates completeness on kept units before the lock; a failure leaves the session unlocked.
Failure evidence identifies the session, the unit reference, the unit kind, the schema and the failed field.
Every authorable kind yields either a checked-valid result, schema findings, writer-validator findings, or an explicit 'not checked' report, never silent clean.
Advisory findings are present on the unit at ratification and do not block unless the kind is promoted by the repository's configuration.
verification: Two passes: the drafting pass checks only value-shape validity of the values a spec already carries (pattern, enum, type, additionalProperties) — these are wrong the instant they are written, so the pass applies to incomplete drafts too; the ratification pass checks only completeness (required, minItems, minLength, minProperties), only on kept units, and only before the session is locked. Drafting is an upsert loop, so an unfinished spec is a draft there and a defect only once the operator asserts the set may be authored.

Disposition policy is owned by this rule, not the profile: enforced kinds raise, and so do kinds the repository promotes to enforced via the stack's exception-declaration mechanism; advisory kinds report and never block — an exception this rule itself authors — and their findings ride on the unit, survive session-history compaction and resurface at ratification.

The enforced/advisory assignment is made by the rule's own criterion: a kind blocks when its schema describes the artifacts the authoring tool actually authors, and reports when that schema has drifted from those artifacts. The stack realization fixes the concrete default assignment for each kind (deriving it by measuring that criterion); the profile supplies only the concrete kind names and the promotion mechanism, never the dispositions.

Every authorable kind is governed: each check outcome is checked-valid, schema findings, the kind's writer-validator findings, or an explicit not-checked report — never a silent clean. A kind whose artifact has no schema is governed by its writer's validator instead.
Atomicity: the ratification pass runs before the lock, so a failure leaves the session unlocked.
The check is confirm-blocking on the plan session (it runs at the confirmation phase); disposition strict, severity 4, applies to enforced and promoted kinds, while advisory kinds only report.
A failure identifies the session, the unit reference, the unit kind, the schema and the failed field.

Not covered: completeness is not enforced on drafts during the drafting phase nor on units dropped before ratification, and artifacts produced by the authoring tool outside a plan session are not re-checked (valid by construction).

fires: The planner adds an ordinary, valid unit of any authorable kind while drafting: it is checked and yields a checked-valid outcome.
The planner ratifies a session: every kept unit is checked for completeness, including units that turn out valid.
The planner adds a unit while drafting whose spec carries a value violating a pattern, enum, type or additionalProperties constraint of its enforced schema.
An incomplete draft that also carries a malformed value: the malformed value is still refused while drafting.
The planner ratifies a session in which a kept unit of an enforced kind is missing a required field or violates minItems/minLength/minProperties.
A unit of an advisory kind violates its schema: findings are reported and carried on the unit to ratification, without blocking.
A repository promotes an advisory kind to enforced in its configuration: violations of that kind now block like an enforced kind.
A unit of a kind with no artifact schema is added: its writer's validator must check it.
A unit of a kind that nothing checks is added: the check must say explicitly that it is not checked, not return clean.
doesNotFire: Completeness enforcement (required, minItems, minLength, minProperties) on an incomplete spec during drafting: incompleteness alone is not a defect in the draft. Well-formedness checking of the values it does carry still fires.
Completeness checking of a unit dropped (not kept) before ratification.
Artifacts generated by the authoring tool outside a plan session (already schema-valid by construction).

neutralityNotes: The schema-constraint keyword lists (pattern, enum, type, additionalProperties vs required, minItems, minLength, minProperties) are kept verbatim as the neutral names for the value-shape/completeness split; a stack with a different schema language maps them to its equivalents. Plan-session phase, operation and state labels (plan:Compose, plan:Ratify, add_unit, ratify, locked) are bound as the plan_session entry of the idiom.plan_syntax map key. The repository's promotion declaration (plan.spec_validation.enforce in .atdd/config.yaml) is bound as the plan_spec_promotion entry of enforcement.exceptions — where and how the stack declares an intentional override of the rule's advisory exception — mechanism only, since promotion behaviour is rule policy. The enforced/advisory dispositions are this rule's own policy: the classification criterion and the strict/confirm-blocking disposition live in core:verification, and the concrete default kind assignments (wagon, train, interlocking, embedded acceptance enforced; feature, wmbt advisory; contract schema-less) are preserved as bunOnly realization data. roles.plan_artifact.kinds binds only the plain list of concrete kind names (as a single string value), with the open-set scope kept in core activation. The 'every authorable kind is governed' obligation is kept inside this core even though bun.json's splitSuggestion would package it as its own rule — dropping it would weaken the core. Empirical conformance measurements, the contract/#2013 forcing example, term ids, validation-taxonomy ids and failure-evidence field ids remain bunOnly. activation.fires/doesNotFire are not numbered items, so they are carried into the core without classification entries.
